role.altitude: The prepress technician keeps arranging pages, judging proofs, deciding plate types and checking settings before output; copying text into layouts, typing job specs into the RIP, filing and searching job folders and comparing proofs by eye shrink.
skills_to_grow: Maintaining preflight profiles and flow rules
role.ambitious_version: A technician whose job data flows from the order to the platesetter, leaving the time for layout and quality.

tasks.short: Import client text and images, enter, position and alter text size to make up and arrange pages, apply client corrections, and preflight the pages.

steps.what: Technician imports client text and images into the page layout
Technician positions elements and alters text size to make up and arrange pages
Technician preflights the finished pages: fonts, resolution, bleed and colour space

tasks.design: A flow automation picks up client files, places text and images into the job's template with the house styles, and the technician checks the result instead of copying and styling by hand. Arranging pages, fitting copy and applying corrections stay with the technician; standard templates auto-fit simple jobs. Preflight profiles check fonts, image resolution, bleed and colour space and log every automatic fix for the proof.
tasks.previous_blocker: Text and images were placed and styled by hand.
tasks.still_hard: Complex layouts with tight copy fitting.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a page reads badly even when every rule passes.
tasks.altitude: Less placing and checking; layout stays.

evidence.claim: Preflight and flow automation software checks and edits PDFs and automates the job flow.
A large-format printer cut banner preparation from about 2 hours to 20-30 minutes; vendor case, no volume given.

assumptions: Boundary: making up pages; scanner settings (task 10428) are a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: client files delivered through the upload portal in agreed formats, about 70% of jobs; s1 is priced at that share.

Corrections keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for checking placed content and for the 30% of jobs that arrive outside the portal; s2 keeps 85 because only simple jobs auto-fit; s4 keeps 30 for reading the preflight log and fixing what it cannot.
research_questions: Does preparation time per job fall?

incremental.description: Technician maintains templates and preflight profiles.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of clients use the portal and few jobs fit a standard template (16.2); high: 70% of jobs through the portal as assumed (25.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter job specifications on computer-aided equipment, store job files, retrieve information and files for reprints, and check settings before output.

steps.what: Technician enters job specifications into the RIP and platesetter
Technician stores job files in the archive
Technician retrieves information and files for reprints
Technician checks the settings before output

tasks.design: The print management system sends the job ticket with size, colours, screening and plate settings to the RIP and platesetter in the standard job format, instead of the technician typing them from the job bag. The flow automation files output by job number and the management system finds them for reprints. The technician still checks the settings before output.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specs were typed from paper job bags and files filed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Job ticket exchange between management system and RIP, and flow automation.
tasks.still_hard: Older equipment without job ticket import.
tasks.human_edge: Catching a setting that is valid but wrong for this paper.
tasks.altitude: Much less typing and filing; checking stays.

reach.learn: Whether job status is known without asking.

evidence.claim: Flow automation software automates the job flow including file handling.
A print management system holds orders, stock and cost; for one printer the vendor projects 42 of 62 admin hours a month saved, not measured.

assumptions: Boundary: entering, storing and retrieving information; making up pages (task 10403) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: the management system and RIP support the standard job ticket format, for about 80% of jobs; s1 is priced at that share.

Checking keeps its full time. s1 keeps 20 for the 20% of jobs on equipment without ticket import; s2 keeps 20 for files outside the flow; s3 keeps 40 for reading the found job and older jobs filed by hand.
unknowns: Share of equipment with job ticket import.
research_questions: Do setting errors at output fall?

incremental.description: Technician maintains job ticket mappings and flow rules.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of the equipment takes the job ticket, so half of the specs are still typed and filed by hand (37.5); high: about 80% of jobs by ticket as assumed (59.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up the proof press, operate presses to print proofs of plates, monitor printing quality, and compare proofs against the approved file.

steps.what: Technician sets up the proof press
Technician operates the press to print proofs of plates
Technician monitors printing quality: colour, registration and defects, with colour bar values from a spectrophotometer after the change
Technician lays the printed proof on the scanner and scans it for the compare
Technician compares the proof against the approved file: side by side today; after the change by reviewing each difference the automated compare flags

tasks.design: Setting up and running the proof press stay hands-on. A spectrophotometer measures the colour bar and flags values outside tolerance, so the technician judges quality with numbers beside the eye. An automated compare of the scanned proof against the approved file flags text, artwork and barcode differences, instead of a side-by-side visual check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Colour and differences were judged by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Colour measurement and automated proof comparison.
tasks.still_hard: Special inks and substrates without reference values.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing mottle or banding no measurement catches.

evidence.claim: Automated proof checks compare text, artwork, spelling and barcodes against the approved file; one packaging firm saved about 10 minutes per job on barcodes alone.

assumptions: Boundary: proofing plates; setting scanners (task 10428) is a sibling task.

Set-up, running and scanning the proof keep their full time. s3 keeps 85 because the colour bar values replace part of the colour judgement while registration and defects are still judged by eye; s4 keeps 40 for reviewing each flagged difference and deciding whether it matters.
unknowns: Share of jobs with colour bars and digital approved files.

incremental.description: Technician maintains colour targets and compare settings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many jobs use special inks without reference values and the compare flags many false differences (5.1); high: standard process colour jobs (12.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read run length, press and paper from the job ticket, check the plate rule table, select proper types of plates according to press run lengths, and pull plates from stock.

steps.what: Technician reads run length, press and paper: from the job bag today, from the job ticket on screen after the change
Technician checks the plate rule table for the run length and press
Technician selects the proper type of plates according to press run lengths

tasks.design: The job ticket in the print management system shows run length, press and paper, and a rule table proposes the plate type for that combination, instead of the technician reading the job bag and recalling the chart. The technician confirms or changes the choice for special cases. Pulling plates from stock keeps its full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job facts were on paper and the plate rules in people's heads.
tasks.enabler_now: Print management systems with rule tables.
tasks.still_hard: Jobs with unusual inks that wear plates faster.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing a reprint will follow and choosing a longer-lasting plate.

reach.learn: Whether plates wear out mid-run less often.

evidence.claim: A print management system holds orders, stock and cost price.

assumptions: Boundary: selecting plates; entering job data on equipment (task 10402) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: the rule table set up once by the prepress lead.

Reading three facts from the job bag is sized at 15 and pulling plates at 35. s1 keeps 50 because reading stays and only finding the facts in the bag goes; s2 keeps 30 for reading the proposal and special cases.
unknowns: Number of plate types in use.
research_questions: Do plate failures on long runs fall?

incremental.description: Technician updates the rule table when plate types change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the rule table covers only the common presses, so half of the jobs are still checked against the chart (11.4); high: the table covers presses and plate types as set up (21.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
